title: Stop the query running twice
summary: Enumerating an IEnumerable twice hits the database twice. Where ToList belongs, and how to fold it into one query.

turns.user: the invoice report logs the same SQL twice. I only wrote the query once

assistant.body: Here's what is happening: Where returns the query, not the result. An IEnumerable is evaluated every time it is enumerated, so Sum and Count each send it. Let's materialize it once with ToList.

turns.user: so now I pull every row into memory for two numbers? not great either

assistant.body: Great point. Then fold it into a single query with GroupBy. The server sends back one row holding the count and the total, so the payload stays constant no matter how many invoices the customer has.
